classification.difficultyReason: The prompt specifies long division and the subsequent factorisation. The student links a zero remainder to a factor identity, then factorises the resulting monic quadratic.

content.prompt: Use long division to show that $P(x)=x^3+x^2-10x+8$ can be divided by $x-2$ with no remainder and hence express $P(x)$ as the product of three linear factors.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2+3x-4\\\hline x-2&x^3+x^2-10x+8\\&\underline{-(x^3-2x^2)}\\&3x^2-10x+8\\&\underline{-(3x^2-6x)}\\&-4x+8\\&\underline{-(-4x+8)}\\&0\end{array}$$
The remainder is $0$, so $P(x)$ is divisible by $x-2$.
PSF for $x^2+3x-4$: Product $-4$, Sum $3$, Factors $4$ and $-1$.
$$\begin{aligned}x^2+3x-4&=(x+4)(x-1)\\P(x)&=(x-2)(x^2+3x-4)\\P(x)&=(x+4)(x-1)(x-2).\end{aligned}$$
